top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock rests on a distinct idea, the magic-wavelength condition that cancels the lattice light shift for many neutral atoms in the Lamb-Dicke regime. It has been reproduced near 1e-18 in several laboratories and species, and it has produced physics: millimetre-scale redshift, bounds on drifting constants and dark matter, and controlled many-body effects. The two-name allocation (Katori for concept and first realisation, Ye for record accuracy and many-body understanding) is defensible, though the chronology rests on recollection and should be checked against primary papers. The citation should name only the lattice clock, to stay distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes. Awarding it is better than no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; as WACQT director I work in superconducting circuits, not optical clocks, so no direct connection to Katori or Ye
